headline: Physical infrastructure toll accelerating as hyperscaler capex overwhelms execution capacity.

deltas.reads: Fiber and data-center infrastructure demand compressing specialty contractor capacity nationwide.
HVAC and mechanical execution work piling up faster than skilled-trades labor can convert it.
Data-center electrical and mechanical construction driving largest RPO growth.
Steel input scarcity lifting margins as data-center and infrastructure projects compete for constrained supply.

deltas.metric: C&I product backlog and sales mix
deltas.reads: Backup-power capacity becoming a hyperscaler constraint; global supply agreements locking in scarce generator output.
Electrical construction capacity tightening as data centers and large-load facilities compete for field labor.

deltas.metric: data-center lease backlog and renewal rent growth
deltas.change: +71% backlog since year-end; +19.3pp renewal rent acceleration
deltas.reads: Hyperscale demand for powered real estate spiking faster than REIT capacity expansion.

momentum_note: All seven companies show acceleration in backlog, margin, or pricing power tied directly to AI infrastructure buildout. Dycom, Comfort Systems, and EMCOR reveal growing labor and execution-capacity constraints in specialty trades. Steel, generation equipment, and data-center real estate all show pricing power or supply tightness. The pattern is consistent: hyperscaler capex is driving demand across the full stack—fiber, electrical, mechanical, power, materials, and facilities—faster than suppliers can expand execution capacity or input availability. This is not cyclical rebound; it is structural toll extraction by scarce physical inputs.
